## 1. Introduction/Context

Working  as  a  pharmacist  carries  significant  responsibilities  and  accountability.  This  is  to ensure safe, legal, evidence based and ethical practice to the highest professional standards. The  public,  patients,  and  healthcare  professionals  trust  pharmacists  because  of  these standards. The role of the pharmacist is also expanding in scope of practice. Each qualified pharmacist must abide by the Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland (PSI) Code of Conduct, 1 which details the professional principles, standards, ethical behaviours, and principles for pharmacy practise. It is also a requirement that during their education pharmacy students abide by the SETU Student Charter and this SETU Master of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct for Student Pharmacists (DOPSOP1). This document was informed by the PSI Code of Conduct for pharmacists, the APPEL Joint Schools of Pharmacy Code of Conduct, required for experiential placement and is informed by and aligned to SETU policies and procedures within its Nursing, Healthcare and Social Care programmes. SETU is committed to providing pharmacy education programmes that demonstrate the highest standards of professional education and training. All students of the Master of Pharmacy (MPharm) are required to complete a Garda Vetting Application  Form  and  have  Garda  clearance  before  clinical  and  professional  practice placements and visits.

On successful completion of the MPharm, the Head of the Department of Pharmacy must make  a  declaration  stating  that  the  student  has  met  all  requirements  to  register  as  a pharmacist,  and  the  PSI  reviews  each  application  to  ensure  that  it  complies  with  the prescribed conditions for registration. This includes qualification, competency, and fitness of an applicant to practise. SETU has a duty of care to protect the public and profession by setting standards  for  education  and  professional  practice  and  acting  when  a  student  pharmacist fitness to practise is in doubt. During their education programme, the pharmacy student is expected  to uphold and display professional standards of behaviour, attitude, and attendance,  which  must  be  displayed  within  SETU,  outside  of  the  University  and  in professional practice settings. The pharmacy student will also abide by the APPEL  Code of Conduct  or  equivalent  in  experiential  placement  settings.  The  term  professional  practice settings  include,  but  is  not  limited  to,  placement  in  a  pharmacy,  industrial  pharmacy  or pharmaceutical setting, or healthcare area, which has been arranged by the University or the student. It also includes any visits, tours or activities organised by the MPharm programme team or University.

## 2. Purpose and Scope

This SETU Master of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct for Student Pharmacists sets out standards, which students must follow in academic, clinical, and professional settings and when interacting with teaching and research staff, students, tutors, patients, carers, and any other member of the public. SETU takes any breach of this Code very seriously and therefore if  standards  are  not  abided  by  the  matter  will  be  referred  to  the  SETU  Department  of Pharmacy Fitness to Practise procedures or SETU disciplinary procedures as required. The SETU Pharmacy Fitness to Practise policy and procedure DOPSOP4 can be found on the Virtual Learning  Environment  in  the  Department  of  Pharmacy,  within  the  Master  of  Pharmacy Information  Area  and  will  be  outlined  at  induction  each  Year.  This  Code  of  Conduct  is underpinned and supported by the SETU Student Expected Behaviour Policy and Disciplinary Policy, SETU  Student  Academic  Misconduct  Policy  and  Disciplinary  Procedure,  SETU Supporting and Determining Students Fitness in Continue Study - Policy and Procedure. It is also  linked  to  Master  of  Pharmacy  Attendance, Academic  Integrity  and Health and  Safety procedures within the Faculty of Science and Computing, the Department of Pharmacy Fitness to Practise policy and procedures and programme Garda Vetting requirements. 2-6

This SETU Master of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct for Student Pharmacists must be formally agreed to by each student each year, through completion of its associated form, and is part of evidence of fitness to practice. It shall be made available and published publicly via the University website and available for students in their handbook.

## 3. Definitions

For the purpose of this policy:

- PSI is defined as Pharmaceutical Society of Ireland, who are the pharmacy regulator in Ireland and are responsible for approving and accrediting pharmacy degree programmes in Ireland.
- APPEL is defined as the Affiliation for Pharmacy Practice Experiential Learning: this collaboration manages the experiential learning placement (ELP) within the integrated pharmacy programmes in Ireland.
- Joint Schools of Pharmacy is defined as a collaboration between the PSI Accredited Schools of Pharmacy in Ireland who deliver a Master of Pharmacy Programme.
- Open Disclosure is the timely communication to patients in an open, honest, and transparent manner when an incident occurs within their care.

## 4. Principles to which Students Adhere

The PSI Code of Conduct sets out seven statutory principles which pharmacy professionals are required to uphold as outlined below. This SETU Master of Pharmacy Professional Code of Conduct  for  Student  Pharmacists-  DOPSOP01  is  set  out  to  align  with  each  principle.  An explanation of each principle adapted from the PSI Code of Conduct, 1 is presented in Table 1, and this  is  related  to  the  requirements  of  students  of  the  MPharm,  and  other  pharmacy related education at SETU.  The Code of Conduct is also aligned to the APPEL Joint Schools of Pharmacy Code of Conduct.

## 5. Principles to be Upheld

The following professional principles must be upheld by all MPharm students.

## 5.1 Principle One: Put the Patient First 1

As a pharmacist, the health, wellbeing, welfare, and safety of the patient should always be put  first.  Patient  dignity  is  paramount,  and  their  values  respected.  The  decision  of  the pharmacist in responding to patients needs should be made based on evidence and should support their decision making and autonomy. The skills, knowledge, behaviours, attributes, and experience built during the pharmacy students' education supports safe and effective practice.  Pharmacists  do  not  all  work  in  contact  with  patients,  but  their  decisions  and behaviour can have a significant impact on patient care.

SETU Pharmacy students must uphold the same ethos, understand this key responsibility, work to build core knowledge and skills and embody professional requirements necessary to become a pharmacist. This holds in both University studies and all professional experiential learning  practice  settings,  placements,  and  visits.  The  health,  safety  and  wellbeing  of  the patient is always paramount.

## Each MPharm student at SETU must therefore:

1. Commit  to  building  their  core  pharmacist  competencies  (knowledge,  skills,  and behaviours) and pharmacist attributes during their studies, taking responsibility for their work and understand the impact of their work in practice to ensure the patient receives safe and effective care.
2. Attend lectures, tutorials, and placement in accordance with the SETU MPharm attendance  procedures  DOPSOP03. 2   100%  attendance  is  required  at  experiential placement, clinical skills elements, and practice visits. 80% attendance is required at all other active learning activities and pharmacy practice lectures. Failure to achieve

- expected attendance levels will be addressed through a 3-stage process outlined in the Master of Pharmacy attendance procedures DOPSOP03. 2
3. Not disrupt the learning experience of fellow students during lectures, seminars, skills, and practice placements.
4. Behave in a responsible, trustworthy, and professional way.
5. Recognise the rights of and treat all others fairly, equally, and with respect, dignity, integrity, and honesty, respecting their values and beliefs as individuals, and rights as patients.
6. Never discriminate against others on the basis of gender, religion, age, civil status and family status, disability, sexual orientation, ethnicity, or membership of the Travelling community.
7. Follow  all  patient  interaction  protocols  during  University  work,  practice  visits, experiential learning professional settings, and placement. These include introduction, supervision,  consent,  professional  boundaries,  patient  autonomy, professional confidentiality, personal data, and records.
8. Review, agree and abide by the APPEL Joint School's Code of Conduct or equivalent always  ensuring  professionalism  and  patient  safety  during  experiential  learning placement.
9. Raise any issues of concern with academic staff, supervisors, preceptors, and tutors, which would compromise or affect student welfare, patient safety, or care.  Report any patient safety incidents immediately. The Master of Pharmacy Student Pharmacists Process for Raising Issues of Concern details information on this process. DOPSOP02. 3  Pharmacy students will be supported in this process.

## 5.2 Principle Two: Act Professionally 1

Pharmacists must always act in a professional manner, with respect, honesty, and integrity. This is important for patients to have trust in their pharmacist and upholds the reputation of pharmacy. The person is always at the center of practice and their needs, beliefs and values carefully considered and supported. In pharmacy education, students must therefore conduct themselves  in  a  professional  manner  in  the  way  that  they  approach  and  complete  their education.  This  is  within  the  University,  outside  and  in  all  professional  and  experiential placement activities.

Each MPharm student at SETU must therefore:

1. Commit to their learning, foster deep learning and application of skills and knowledge.
2. Manage  their  time,  planning  for  and  engaging  in  assessments,  completing,  and submitting practical reports and assignments on time, and with the highest standards of integrity.
3. Abide and clearly follow the University and Faculty of Science and Computing Health and Safety procedures. 4
4. Abide by University, Faculty and Department policy, and lecturer guidelines on the use

of  Generative  AI  or  other  platforms  in  assignments.  Cite  appropriately  academic sources, paraphrasing and applying best practise in academic writing, following SETU policy on Academic Integrity. 5

5. Accurately,  truthfully,  and  honestly  collate  data  from  practicals,  case  studies,  and research work, applying best practice in data management, representation of results and reporting.
6. Manage their health and wellbeing, seeking support if necessary.
7. Declare any conflict of interest.
8. Abide by SETU IT policies: including  SETU Acceptable Usage Policy and SETU Email policy,  communicating with staff, tutors, and fellow students in a professional and personal capacity appropriately and responsibly through email, with the principles of dignity and respect as outlined in SETU Dignity and Respect Policy for Students.  The student must carefully consider their online profile.
9. Responsibly use social media sites, having due regard to the rights and reputation of SETU, placement sites, and others. The student pharmacist must not bring SETU or their placement sites or themselves into disrepute through their use of social media.
10. Adhere  to  the  pharmacy  professional  dress  code  required,  for  university  practice teaching activities and professional environments. Details of this will be provided in the MPharm Pharmacy Practice modules.
11. Understand that dishonesty, indecency, harassment, bullying, violence, and abuse of drugs or alcohol will lead to disciplinary action.
12. Obey the law and inform the University immediately if they are the subject of criminal legal proceedings.
13. Never falsify the signatures of others on any documentation.
14. Respect confidentiality in all forms with respect to educational, professional practice settings and most importantly patient care. This includes documentation, interviews, media, and social media.
15. Vaccination  Alert  for  all  Student  Pharmacists: As  student  pharmacists,  access  to educational opportunities in some healthcare settings may not be granted to student pharmacists if they are not vaccinated and will not agree to vaccination, which is not otherwise  contraindicated.  This  may  delay  progression  through  the  pharmacy programme at SETU. As student pharmacists, vaccinations are advocated not only in the interest of the individual student but also as a protection for health service users and workers, some of whom may have medical vulnerabilities.

## 5.3 Principle Three: Communicate Effectively 1

Communication is a vital skill  in pharmacy to interact with patients, the public and other professionals. This ensures safe, effective care. Each pharmacist must ask questions, listen
